statement: Collaboration Bar shares a model by private invite with access levels or public link with General Access; saves to Trimble Connect first.
superiority: Granular roles with expiry and audit log.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/collaborate-sketchup Acceptance sketch: Invite two users with Comment and View Scenes; permissions enforced on each action.

statement: Owner, View Scenes and Comment permissions for invitees and General Access settings with request-access flow.

source.ref: Access levels: private invite Owner, View Scenes, Comment; General Access No Access, View Scenes, View Model (request flow)

superiority: Per-object and per-tag permissions with time-limited links and an audit trail.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sharing-model Acceptance sketch: Role matrix: 5 roles by 5 actions (view, navigate, measure, comment, edit); each cell allowed or denied as documented.

statement: Viewers see updates in real time with cursors and tool hints and a camera follow.
superiority: Operation-based sync with sub-second latency globally.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Edit changes appear to a viewer within 1 s on LAN; cursor positions agree.

statement: Comments markers in 3D with threads, replies, images, links, and camera/scene association; panel shows threads and hide markers.
superiority: Comments anchored to topological entities that survive edits (BCF export).
notes: Acceptance sketch: Place a comment, reply, resolve; scene and camera restored on click.

statement: Multiple editors edit the same model on the web with an enable toggle; off means a single editor.
superiority: Co-editing on desktop with operation log merge and optional locks.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Two simulated editors add disjoint geometry; merged result contains both with no loss.

statement: Models save to Trimble Connect with file status and unlimited storage in Pro plans.

source.ref: Trimble Connect storage and file status

superiority: Local-first sync with branching, merging and offline edits.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup-subscriptions Acceptance sketch: Save to cloud, make a change, save again, restore the first version; the restored model hash equals the first save.

statement: 3D Warehouse offers search, download, upload and organization sharing of models.
superiority: Provenance and license metadata on every asset.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/3d-warehouse/searching-and-downloading-models https://help.sketchup.com/en/3d-warehouse/uploading-models Acceptance sketch: Search term returns results; upload and re-download is identical.

statement: Collections group models for sharing and saving.
superiority: Collections can be shared with roles and pinned to projects.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/collections-3d-warehouse Acceptance sketch: Create a collection, add 3 models, delete one, delete the collection; membership matches after each step.

statement: Product catalogs, certified content, organization accounts.

source.ref: 3D Warehouse: catalogs, certified content and organizations

superiority: Catalog items validate against a schema (dimensions, IFC class, licence) at upload.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/3d-warehouse/certified-content https://help.sketchup.com/en/3d-warehouse-register-organization Acceptance sketch: Upload a catalog item with metadata and download it; metadata fields round-trip unchanged.

statement: Materials and environments libraries.
superiority: Materials carry measured physical parameters and licence information.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/3d-warehouse/environments-3d-warehouse Acceptance sketch: Download a material from the library; PBR maps and tiling dimensions are intact on import.

statement: Content and download policies govern use.

source.ref: 3D Warehouse content policy and download policy

superiority: Automated pre-publication quality checks with fix suggestions.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/3d-warehouse-download-policy Acceptance sketch: Upload a model violating a stated rule (oversize or stray geometry); the pre-check flags it before publish.

statement: Browser client with modeling, styles, environments, materials, shortcuts, settings.
superiority: Same engine and feature set on web as on desktop, so no capability gap exists.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup-web-shortcuts https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup-web-app-settings Acceptance sketch: Open a desktop-saved model in the web client, edit a face with Push/Pull and save; desktop reopens it with the edit and no loss.

statement: iPad client with Apple Pencil, assistant and measurement.
superiority: Tablet and pen input is a first-class mode of the same application.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup-assistant-ipad Acceptance sketch: Open the same model on iPad, draw with Apple Pencil, save; geometry matches a scripted desktop equivalent within 1e-6.

statement: Meta Quest viewing lets users move through a model at full scale with scenes, tags and Entity Info; the Quest viewer stopped being downloadable on 16 September 2025.
superiority: Streaming with LOD for models far above the 250k triangle guidance.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/spatial-preview Acceptance sketch: Stream a model of 200,000 triangles to a headset; frame rate stays at the device target and the model scale is 1:1 within 1 percent.

statement: Web authoring of Live Components.
superiority: Same authoring is available offline in the desktop app.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Create a parametric component in the web tool, import it to desktop, change one parameter; geometry equals the closed-form size.

statement: Plan types, admin console, seat management, roles, SSO.
superiority: Open-standard SSO and SCIM provisioning with audit logs.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/accounts-and-administration/axp-managing-roles https://help.sketchup.com/en/accounts-and-administration/axp-seat-management Acceptance sketch: Add a seat, assign a product, change a role; each admin action is reflected in the member list and entitlements.

statement: The login-frequency page explains that SketchUp re-validates the licence about every 28 days and gives Windows and macOS steps for repeated sign-in prompts and offline use.

source.ref: Licensing, sign-in, offline use and MFA

superiority: Permanent offline licence option for secured environments.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/authenticator-app https://help.sketchup.com/en/passkeys Acceptance sketch: Disconnect the network; the app keeps working for the documented offline window and warns before expiry.

statement: Revit import and exchange.
superiority: Native Revit read through a licensed route with round-trip write-back.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/revit-version-compatibility Acceptance sketch: Import a sample Revit file; element count, levels and phases equal those reported by the source, and metadata fields are present.

statement: SketchUp Viewer for Desktop stopped being offered for download from 22 April 2025; Trimble Connect, Link Sharing (opened in SketchUp for Web) and the Trimble Connect Visualizer replace it.

source.ref: SketchUp Viewer for Desktop end of support and replacements

superiority: Dino opens a shared link in a browser viewer with no install and no sign-in for view-only access.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Publish a model, create a link and open it in a clean browser profile; the model displays and cannot be edited.

statement: Browsing 3D Warehouse needs no sign-in but sharing or downloading needs a Trimble ID, and Edit Profile and Settings opens Public Profile (display name, links to Trimble and SketchUp profiles), Website and Social, and Preferences sections.
superiority: Profile edits are previewed as other users see them before saving.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Sign in, change the display name and a social link, save, and view the public profile as an anonymous user.

statement: From My Content an uploaded model can be edited: replace the file, set a custom thumbnail, change title, description, external URL, category and subcategory, or delete the model permanently.
superiority: Replacing the file keeps the model URL, ratings and download count.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Upload a model, replace its file and thumbnail and change the title; the details page shows the new values.

statement: An uploaded material can be edited (title, description, category, settings); Convert to Photorealistic adds AI-generated texture maps to a material that has none, and Revert to Original removes only those added maps.
superiority: Conversion is non-destructive and reversible at any time for a material that is later edited.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Upload a material without maps, convert, check maps exist, revert, and check only the added maps are removed.

statement: A model, including one from an older unsupported SketchUp version, can be uploaded in a web browser by signing in, dragging in the file, filling the Edit Model Details dialog (title, description, categories) and choosing Publish Model.
superiority: The discoverability meter shown during upload is computed from specific filled fields and listed.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Upload a sample .skp from a browser; it appears under My Models with the entered title and categories.

statement: Faces should have the white front color outward and the blue back color inward; Orient Faces makes adjacent faces consistent and Reverse Faces fixes separate faces.
superiority: A pre-upload check lists reversed faces by count and location.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Build a closed box with 2 reversed faces; Orient Faces leaves all front faces outward and the check reports zero reversed faces.

statement: Keeping polygon count low means minimal arc and circle segmentation, removing unseen internal geometry, purging unused geometry and softening or smoothing edges instead of hiding them.
superiority: A pre-upload report shows face and edge counts and the saving from each action.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Model a bolt with 24 and 12 segment circles, purge and soften; face count drops and the shape matches within the stated tolerance.

statement: Before upload the model is imported into a new file and checked for thumbnail, attachment to faces, insertion point, tight bounding box, Move tool use, material application and easy editing.

source.ref: 3D Warehouse guideline: testing for correct behavior

superiority: The pre-upload check runs these seven checks automatically and reports pass or fail for each.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Import a sample component into a clean file; all seven listed checks pass and a tight bounding box equals the geometry extents.

statement: Floating and stray geometry should be deleted before upload: show all tags, toggle Hidden Geometry and Zoom Extents to find it, because stray geometry enlarges the uploaded content bounding box.
superiority: The pre-upload check names every stray edge and face and shows the bounding box change from removing them.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Add one stray edge far from a model; Zoom Extents shows it, deleting it shrinks the bounding box back to the model extents.

statement: A component axes origin defaults to the lower-left corner of the selection bounding box and sets both the placement point on download from 3D Warehouse and the reference point when the component is replaced or reloaded, so it should sit on the ground plane at a governing point.

source.ref: 3D Warehouse guideline: axes and origin points

superiority: The check warns when the origin is not on the object ground plane.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Set the origin of a lamp component at its base center and place it; the base center lands at the click point.
